title: Regular characteristic-zero affinoids remain regular after complete field extension
statement:
Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field complete for a nontrivial discrete nonarchimedean absolute value, let $r,s\geq0$, and let $A=K\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ be the Tate algebra: its elements are series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}a_
u x^
u$ such that for each $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many $
u$ satisfy $|a_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Choose $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in A$, put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ and $C=A/I$, and suppose $C$ is a regular Noetherian ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every isometric field embedding $K\hookrightarrow L$ into a complete nonarchimedean field with a real-valued absolute value, let $f_{j,L}\in L\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ be obtained by applying this embedding to all coefficients. Then $C_L=L\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle/(f_{1,L},\ldots,f_{s,L})$ is a regular Noetherian ring. The zero quotient and $r=0$ or $s=0$ are included.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof, printed p.19: regular affinoids over a perfect complete field are smooth; formulated as regularity after analytic scalar extension. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of equal size, write $I_E=(f_j:j\in E)$ and $D_{E,U}=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i\in U,j\in E}$. The derivatives preserve restricted series because $|n|\leq1$ for integers $n$, and satisfy Leibniz coefficientwise. Put $H=\sum_{E,U}\overline{(I_E:I)}\,\bar D_{E,U}C$. Characteristic zero makes $K$ perfect: the derivative of any nonconstant irreducible polynomial is nonzero and relatively prime to that polynomial. Apply [lem-per-perfect-affinoid-local-jacobian-chart] to the given regular Noetherian $C$. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C$ it supplies $a\in(I_E:I)$ with $\bar a\bar D_{E,U}\notin\mathfrak m$. Thus $H$ is contained in no maximal ideal.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof and Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.19--21; explicit coefficient-extension argument by Q63

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], a proper ideal of $C$ would be contained in a maximal ideal. Hence $H=C$. Membership of $1$ in this sum of ideals means that for finitely many triples $(a_\lambda,E_\lambda,U_\lambda)$ and $b_\lambda\in C$,
$$1=\sum_\lambda b_\lambda\bar a_\lambda\bar D_{E_\lambda,U_\lambda},\qquad a_\lambda I\subseteq I_{E_\lambda}.$$
This formulation also works for $C=0$, with the empty sum.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof and Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.19--21; explicit coefficient-extension argument by Q63

proof.text: Fix the stated extension $K\hookrightarrow L$. Applying the embedding to coefficients defines a homomorphism $A\to A_L=L\langle x\rangle$: isometry preserves the restricted condition, and each coefficient of a product is a finite sum. Since $f_j\mapsto f_{j,L}$, this induces $C\to C_L$. For every $\lambda,j$, write $a_\lambda f_j=\sum_{e\in E_\lambda}q_{\lambda je}f_e$ in $A$. Extending these finitely many identities gives $a_{\lambda,L}I_L\subseteq I_{E_\lambda,L}$. Termwise differentiation commutes with coefficient extension since integer scalars are fixed. The finite permutation formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] therefore gives $(D_{E,U})_L=D^L_{E,U}$. Extending the identity in Step 2 now gives $1=\sum_\lambda b_{\lambda,L}\bar a_{\lambda,L}\bar D^L_{E_\lambda,U_\lambda}$ in $C_L$. Every summand belongs to its analytic Jacobian ideal $H_L$, so $H_L=C_L$. Only inclusion of extended colon elements is used, with no flatness or colon base-change equality asserted.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof and Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.19--21; explicit coefficient-extension argument by Q63

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-affinoid-jacobian-certificate-regular] over $L$ to the restricted series $f_{1,L},\ldots,f_{s,L}$ and the unit certificate $H_L=C_L$ of Step 3. The absolute value on $L$ is nontrivial because it extends the nontrivial one on $K$, and it is complete and real-valued by hypothesis; discreteness of $L$ is not needed. The lemma gives exactly that $C_L$ is regular Noetherian, including the zero quotient and empty lists of equations or variables.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-ed71a6377 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and both new nodes in full, plus the cited statements: def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant, and lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal (Mathlib Ideal.exists_le_maximal). Also read the citer regular-generic-continuous-jacobian and the neighbouring nodes. The item statement is byte-identical to the Q06 base, and there is no repair note, so this is a first split. Temkin 3.3.1/3.3.2 is not in literature/ and is listed as WANTED; proof_origin is agent, which is correct. Because I could not read the source, I checked the mathematics directly. Step 1: char 0 implies perfect, and perfect-affinoid-local-jacobian-chart gives a⋅D̄ ∉ 𝔪 at every maximal ideal. Step 2: the proper-ideal leaf gives H=C as a finite identity, including C=0. Step 3 (elementary): coefficient extension is a ring map, the colon relations transfer, derivatives and the Leibniz determinant commute with it, so H_L=C_L. Only colon inclusion is used. Step 4: certificate-regular applied over L, which is nontrivial because it restricts to K. New node local-jacobian-chart is true: k(𝔫) is finite separable, F[x] surjects onto T/𝔫², so 𝔫/𝔫² → k(𝔫)^r is injective. The regular quotient then gives E with I_𝔫=(f_E)_𝔫, an element a ∉ 𝔫 and a minor ∉ 𝔫. Perfectness is necessary: x^p−a over an imperfect field has no certificate. New node certificate-regular is true in every characteristic: independent df_j means the f_j are part of a regular system of parameters of T_𝔫. Edge cases B=0, r=0, s=0 are fine. Both new nodes are statement-only, self-contained, carry four search kinds, and use the item's unit. Neither is a duplicate: geometric-affinoid-jacobian-unit has the item's conclusion as its hypothesis, and the polynomial, étale and torsion Jacobian nodes differ. Neither restates the item, and there is no cycle. The route is within the unit, with Mathlib leaves only, so no tool_uses. No fixes. Maintainer note: the citer could get H_K=C directly from local-jacobian-chart plus the maximal-ideal argument, without going through this item and geometric-affinoid-jacobian-unit.
